documents.title: Integration guides
documents.body: Start here if you are wiring Senkronla into your product for the first time. It is open source and self-hosted — run the relay on your own servers. We explain every concept in plain language; you do not need to know our codebase beforehand.

documents.title: Core concepts
documents.body: Core concepts Senkronla syncs JSON snapshots per customer workspace — one or more named documents per namespace. These terms appear throughout the SDK and API: Who does what? Your app owns the user experience and data model. Senkronla owns transport: storing opaque packages, versioning, device slots, and notifying other clients. A workspace — one isolated sync space, usually one per customer account. Identified by a UUID v4 you choose or generate. Secret string returned when a device is created or paired. Send as Bearer token on every API call. The SDK stores it in EsrStorage. UUID generated once on the client and kept forever. Identifies this physical install inside envelopes — different from the server deviceId (ULID). 24-word BIP39 phrase shown once at workspace creation. Proves ownership if all devices are lost. Never sent to the server — only a hash proof. ULID version tag on each snapshot. Required for optimistic locking on push — mismatch returns REVISION_CONFLICT. ESR-DOC1 wrapper around your JSON snapshot plus metadata. The relay stores it but does not parse your app data. A named snapshot in a namespace (documentId, e.g. primary, settings). Each has its own revision chain. Default document id. Single-document apps use only primary (schemaVersion: 1). Additional ids use schemaVersion: 2. Six-digit code valid for a few minutes. Host device generates it; guest device redeems it to join the workspace.

documents.title: Integration checklist
documents.body: Integration checklist Work through this list before shipping to production: Get your relay URL You need a running Senkronla relay. Follow the ESR setup guide or use for this documentation. Install the SDK Add @senkronla/client to your app (or plan REST calls for non-JS clients). Implement DocumentAdapter exportDocument / importDocument must round-trip your app state as JSON. Keep exports fast — they run before every push. Handle recovery UI onRecoveryPhrase fires once. Build a modal with copy/save — you cannot retrieve the phrase later. Handle conflicts onConflict must ask the user to keep local or remote. There is no automatic merge. Wire the sync loop ensureNamespace() → sync() on startup (all documents) → notifyLocalChange(documentId?) after edits → flushPush(documentId?) before logout. Register your app (when relay requires it) If the operator enabled apps.enabled, obtain an appId, complete origin or bundle approval, and pass app fields to EsrSync.connect(). See <sdkAppLink>SDK — Application registry</sdkAppLink>.

documents.title: Multiple documents in one workspace
documents.body: Multiple documents in one workspace Use this when app data and settings (or other independent JSON blobs) should sync separately under the same namespaceId. Pass a documents array to EsrSync.connect (optional documentId per slot, e.g. settings). Each slot needs its own adapter; all must return the same namespaceId(). Full SDK reference →

documents.title: First device in a workspace
documents.body: First device in a workspace This is the path for a brand-new customer who has no synced data yet: Complete minimal setup After ensureNamespace(), the device token and revision state live in EsrStorage — users do not manage tokens manually. Pick a stable namespaceId Use your internal customer/workspace UUID. It must stay the same across app reinstalls if you want the same sync space. Create the adapter Point exportDocument at your store snapshot and importDocument at your restore logic. Connect EsrSync Pass relayUrl, document, storage, and the required callbacks. Call ensureNamespace() Creates the workspace on first run, shows recovery phrase, performs initial push. Hook local changes Call notifyLocalChange('primary') (or your documentId) whenever that store mutates. The SDK debounces pushes (default 2 seconds).

documents.title: Add a second device
documents.body: Add a second device The guest device needs the same namespaceId in its adapter but does not have a token yet. Host (has data) Guest (new device) Host calls startPairing() Display the 6-digit code and optional QR (qrPayload uses esr://pair/v1/...). Guest calls joinPairing(code) Receives a device token, stores it, and runs sync() to download all documents. Verify slot limits If the workspace is full, pairing returns DEVICE_LIMIT_*. Surface your upgrade UI via onDeviceLimit.

documents.title: When all devices are lost
documents.body: When all devices are lost The user enters their 24-word recovery phrase. The SDK builds a cryptographic proof and calls the recover endpoint. Important side effect Recovery revokes every previously paired device. All other phones and laptops lose access until paired again. Collect the phrase Normalize whitespace; the SDK handles casing. Call sync.recover(phrase) Call sync.recover(phrase) — stores a fresh device token for this install. Run sync(documentId?) sync() pulls and pushes every connected document; sync(documentId) targets one slot (e.g. settings).

documents.title: Offline edits and conflicts
documents.body: Offline edits and conflicts Senkronla is offline-friendly by design. The SDK queues local changes and syncs when the network returns. No server-side merge If two devices edit offline and both push, the second push gets REVISION_CONFLICT. Your onConflict callback decides the winner — plan UI copy accordingly. User edits offline Save locally as usual, then call notifyLocalChange(). Status may show offline or pending_push. Network returns Scheduler or manual sync() (all documents) or sync(documentId) attempts push/pull. Conflict detected onConflict receives documentId and remoteMeta. Return remote, local, or cancel per document.

documents.title: Device limits in your UI
documents.body: Device limits in your UI Each workspace has maxDevices = free slots + purchased slots. Your product decides what happens when the limit is hit: DEVICE_LIMIT_PAYMENT_REQUIRED — show upgrade / unlock flow (onDeviceLimit callback). DEVICE_LIMIT_BLOCKED — hard cap; user must revoke an old device via listDevices() + revokeDevice(). Unlock codes from your operator are redeemed with redeemUnlockCode().

documents.title: SDK or REST?
documents.body: SDK or REST? Use the SDK unless you have a strong reason not to — it saves weeks of edge-case handling. JavaScript SDK (recommended) Browser, Electron, React Native (with fetch), Node 18+. Handles tokens, debounce, WS notifications, conflicts. REST API directly Swift, Kotlin, server jobs, or custom sync engines. You implement revision checks, token storage, and notification polling yourself. Reference: SDK docs API docs

documents.title: ESR setup guide
documents.body: Deploy the Envelope Sync Relay (ESR) on your own infrastructure. After the API is running, point your app at and follow the integration guides.

documents.title: What you are deploying
documents.body: What you are deploying Senkronla ESR is a self-hosted relay API. It stores opaque ESR-DOC1 envelopes, coordinates revisions, manages device pairing, and enforces slot limits — without reading your app payload. REST API under /v1 plus optional WebSocket notifications PostgreSQL for metadata and a filesystem volume for blob storage Operator tools: admin API, CLI unlock codes, and the web operator portal

documents.title: Prerequisites
documents.body: Prerequisites Before you deploy, prepare: PostgreSQL 16+ (bundled via Docker Compose or your own instance) Persistent storage for blobs (ESR_BLOB_PATH) Long random secrets for ESR_ADMIN_TOKEN (min 32 characters) TLS termination in production (Caddy, nginx, or a cloud load balancer)

documents.title: Docker Compose (recommended)
documents.body: Docker Compose (recommended) The fastest path for a full stack — API, web portal, and optional bundled Postgres: Bundled Postgres Existing Postgres Point ESR_DATABASE_URL at your instance and start without the bundled database profile: Web portal The compose file also starts the docs portal on port 3000. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL to your public relay URL (e.g. https://yourdomain.com). Copy environment file Start from docker/.env.example and set secrets before production. Choose database mode Use --profile bundled-db for a local Postgres container, or set ESR_DATABASE_URL for an external database. Start services Migrations run automatically on API startup. API listens on port 8080 by default.

documents.title: Local development (monorepo)
documents.body: Local development (monorepo) Run from source when you are contributing or debugging the relay itself: API: port 8080 · Swagger UI: /docs · Web portal: port 3000. Migrations also run on startup; run pnpm --filter @senkronla/server migrate manually if needed. Install dependencies Requires Node.js 22+ and pnpm 9+. Start Postgres Use Docker Compose for a bundled database, or point ESR_DATABASE_URL in .env at your instance. Configure secrets Copy .env.example to .env and set ESR_ADMIN_TOKEN and other values. Run dev servers pnpm dev starts the API and web portal together.

documents.title: Key configuration
documents.body: Key configuration Environment variables override packages/server/config.example.yaml. Common settings: Production secrets Never commit real tokens. Rotate ESR_ADMIN_TOKEN if leaked — it gates all admin and operator portal access. PostgreSQL connection string Public base URL (used in CLI, portal, and CORS checks) Bearer token for admin API and operator portal login Filesystem path for encrypted envelope blobs Free device slots per namespace (default 2) payment or block when the device limit is reached Comma-separated allowed origins — avoid * in production Max documents per namespace ( default 32, 0 = unlimited) Optional comma-separated document ID allowlist (e.g. primary,settings) ESR_APPS__ENABLED — enable app registry (default false) ESR_APPS__REGISTRATION_MODE — operator_managed or self_service ESR_APPS__ALLOW_LOCALHOST_ORIGINS — allow http://localhost without DNS verify (dev only) ESR_APPS__NATIVE__REQUIRE_CLIENT_SECRET — require X-ESR-Client-Secret on unauthenticated routes ESR_APPS__NATIVE__REQUIRE_MANUAL_REVIEW — operator must approve native bundles before app becomes active (default true) ESR_DEVELOPER_JWT_SECRET — min 32 chars; required for /developer portal when self-service

documents.title: Rate limits
documents.body: Rate limits The relay protects shared infrastructure with sliding-window quotas stored in PostgreSQL. Limits are on by default (limits.rateLimit.enabled: true). When a quota is exhausted the API returns 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Exempt from the general IP quota: /health, /metrics, and WebSocket .../notifications. Routes under /v1/admin are not rate-limited. Default quotas Configuration Set values in packages/server/config.example.yaml under limits.rateLimit, or override with environment variables: Reverse proxy The general IP quota uses the client address. Behind nginx, Caddy, or a cloud load balancer, enable server.trustProxy: true or ESR_TRUST_PROXY=true so counters see the real client IP — not the proxy hop. Per-app limits (app registry) When apps.enabled is true, POST /v1/namespaces enforces a separate namespace_create quota (default 100 / day / app). Per-app YAML under apps.limits.perApp can also cap recover and pairing-token rates before namespace-level overrides apply. Operator overrides In the operator portal, use the Limits action on a namespace, app, or developer to override individual quotas without restarting the relay. Effective value resolution: namespace → app → developer → config. Full spec: <limitsSpecLink>17-OPERATOR-LIMIT-OVERRIDES</limitsSpecLink>. Monitoring The operator console Rate limits tab groups recent hits by action (put_document, recover, pair_device, namespace_create, etc.) with namespace, device, and IP context. Client-facing responses App integrators should honor Retry-After, RateLimit-* headers, and optional JSON rateLimits objects on success responses. See the <apiLink>REST API — Relay quotas</apiLink> section for header names, body shapes, and examples. All /v1 requests Document push Guest pairing redeem Pairing code generation Recovery phrase Namespace create 300 / minute 120 / hour 20 / hour 30 / hour 5 / hour 100 / day Client IP Device Namespace Namespace Namespace App + client IP 1 minute 1 hour 1 hour 1 hour 1 hour 24 hours Master switch — set false only for isolated test environments Recovery attempts per namespace per hour Guest pairing redeems per namespace per hour Pairing codes generated per namespace per hour Document pushes per device per hour (every successful PUT counts) Total /v1 requests per client IP per minute Trust X-Forwarded-For when behind a reverse proxy Namespace creates per app per day (namespace_create) Optional per-app cap on recovery (overrides global default when lower in cascade) Optional per-app cap on pairing codes

documents.title: Verify the deployment
documents.body: Verify the deployment Confirm the relay is healthy before wiring your app: Open /docs for interactive Swagger UI. Set your SDK relayUrl to (must end with /v1). Health check GET /health should return 200 when database and blob storage are reachable. Check Swagger Browse /docs to confirm the API surface matches your integration plan. Smoke test Create a namespace from your app or run the SDK quick-start against this relay URL.

documents.title: Production checklist
documents.body: Production checklist Before serving real users: Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and set ESR_PUBLIC_URL to your HTTPS origin (e.g. https://yourdomain.com) Enable server.trustProxy: true (or equivalent) so rate limits use the client IP Restrict ESR_CORS_ORIGINS to your app domains Schedule Postgres backups and snapshot the blob volume When enabling app registry: register apps, verify origins, set legacyDefaultAppId for existing namespaces — see <specLink>16-APP-REGISTRY §19</specLink> Unlock codes After manual payment or support verification, generate slot unlock codes with the CLI (requires ESR_ADMIN_TOKEN):

documents.title: Next steps
documents.body: Next steps Relay is running — wire your product: Integration guide SDK reference REST API

documents.title: Agents guide
documents.body: Give AI coding agents focused Markdown files for SDK or REST integration — overview plus split references, without relay deployment noise.

documents.title: Why agent docs?
documents.body: Why agent docs? Human guides on this site are great for learning, but coding agents work best with dense, link-stable Markdown files they can fetch per stack (SDK vs REST). SDK integration via @senkronla/client and EsrSync REST bootstrap, push/pull, pairing, and error codes under /v1 Pointers to full human docs when the agent needs more detail

documents.title: How agent docs work (May 2026)
documents.body: How agent docs work (May 2026) Two complementary conventions emerged for AI discoverability — use the right one for your audience: llms.txt (website manifest) Proposed at llmstxt.org and widely adopted by documentation sites (Anthropic, Stripe, Cloudflare, Cursor, and others). Place /llms.txt at your site root: a short Markdown index with curated links to the best files for inference-time lookup. Optional ## Optional section marks secondary links agents may skip when context is tight. AGENTS.md (repository onboarding) Stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation). An AGENTS.md in a repo root tells coding agents how to build, test, and follow conventions inside that codebase. Closest file in the tree wins — useful for monorepos, not for public product docs. What Senkronla publishes This portal ships llms.txt plus split agent files: overview (en.md / tr.md), SDK reference (sdk-en.md / sdk-tr.md), and REST API reference (api-en.md / api-tr.md). ESR deployment stays in the human ESR guide.

documents.title: Download or link
documents.body: Download or link Fetch these URLs from your deployment origin (prepend your portal hostname if the agent runs off-site). Split by stack so agents load only what they need: Overview /agents/en.md English — architecture, checklist, concepts /agents/tr.md Turkish — mimari, kontrol listesi, kavramlar SDK reference /agents/sdk-en.md English — @senkronla/client, EsrSync, multi-document /agents/sdk-tr.md Turkish — SDK entegrasyon referansı REST API reference /agents/api-en.md English — /v1 HTTP, envelopes, WebSocket, errors /agents/api-tr.md Turkish — REST API referansı Site manifest /llms.txt Site manifest listing all agent and human doc links Recommended: fetch /llms.txt, then /agents/en.md (or tr.md) plus sdk-en.md or api-en.md for your stack. English agents: sdk-en.md + api-en.md. Turkish: sdk-tr.md + api-tr.md.

documents.title: Feeding files to agents
documents.body: Feeding files to agents Copy the Markdown URL into your agent context, or paste the raw file at the start of a session: Cursor / Copilot / Claude Code Add the agent Markdown URL to project docs, or @-mention the fetched file in chat. For repos, you can symlink or copy content into AGENTS.md — but keep the portal URL canonical for non-repo workflows. Custom automation Fetch /llms.txt first, then /agents/en.md (overview) and /agents/sdk-en.md or /agents/api-en.md for your stack. Turkish: /agents/tr.md, /agents/sdk-tr.md, /agents/api-tr.md. Relay URL Agent files use placeholder relay URLs. Replace with your deployment's /v1 base before generating integration code. Keep context small Start with the agent file alone. Open /sdk or /api human reference only for method signatures, quotas, or exhaustive error lists.

documents.title: In scope vs out of scope
documents.body: In scope vs out of scope Agent files target application integrators: In: EsrSync.connect, adapters, sync loop, pairing, recovery, REST namespace bootstrap In: Required callbacks, revision conflicts, device limits, key error codes Out: Docker Compose, Postgres, ESR_* env vars, unlock codes, operator portal Out: Relay deployment — see human /guides/esr instead If the task is "deploy Senkronla on a server", use the ESR setup guide, not the agent integration file.

documents.title: Human docs
documents.body: Human docs Agents file is a shortcut — your team still has full references: Integration guides SDK reference REST API

documents.title: Client SDK reference
documents.body: Package: @senkronla/client. The EsrSync class is your main entry point — it wraps HTTP, optional WebSocket notifications, local revision tracking, and user-facing callbacks.

documents.title: App code vs the SDK
documents.body: App code vs the SDK Senkronla stores opaque JSON snapshots — it does not ship the app's data model, UI, or billing screens. Samples use placeholder names (appStore, appUi, appSession); they are not part of @senkronla/client. Replace them with the app's modules. Reading code samples Lines marked // app: or names like appStore / appUi — the host application. EsrSync, createDocumentAdapter, notifyLocalChange, etc. — provided by the SDK. Responsibility split Document adapter Workspace id Recovery phrase UX Conflict UX Device limit UX Sync indicators Local edit wiring Pairing screens Sync password Local persistence Relay connection exportDocument / importDocument — serialize and apply app state as JSON Stable UUID per customer workspace; persist before ensureNamespace() onRecoveryPhrase — modal to copy/save the 24-word phrase (required, once) onConflict — ask user; return remote, local, or cancel (required) onDeviceLimit — open upgrade / revoke UI when slots are full (optional) onStatusChange, onDocumentStatusChange — badges or spinners (optional) After local edits, call notifyLocalChange(documentId?) from appStore (or equivalent listener) Show code / qrPayload from startPairing(); guest enters code for joinPairing() resolvePassword() or manual buildEnvelope password — appSession, keychain, or prompt EsrStorage implementation or createLocalStorageAdapter; secure storage on mobile relayUrl, appId, native fields from the relay operator Wraps app-provided functions; calls them on push/pull Sends id to relay; binds namespace to app when registry enabled Generates phrase at workspace creation; invokes the app callback Detects revision mismatch; pauses until the app chooses Surfaces DEVICE_LIMIT_* errors with slot package hints Reports idle, syncing, conflict, offline, … Debounced push queue (default 2s) Creates pairing token; returns code, QR payload, expiry Builds ENV-ENC1 envelopes on push; decrypts on pull Persists deviceToken, per-document revisions, optional recovery phrase HTTP + WebSocket client to the relay

documents.title: Quick start
documents.body: Quick start Copy the template below. Replace appStore / appUi with the app's modules and set appId to your registered app: Application registry When GET /health reports apps.enabled: true, appId is required on every relay request. Register the app and verify origin (web) or bundle (native) before calling the API — see <appRegistryLink>Application registry</appRegistryLink>. Omit appId only when the relay keeps apps.enabled: false (v1.2 legacy). Relay URL for this deployment Set relayUrl to or read it from your own config.

documents.title: Install
documents.body: Install Requires Node 18+ or a modern browser with fetch and Web Crypto. @senkronla/client includes TypeScript types and everything needed for a typical EsrSync integration. The SDK builds and decrypts ESR-DOC1 / ENV-ENC1 envelopes on push and pull — you do not need a second package for that path. REST-only integrations Add @senkronla/protocol when you call the relay over HTTP yourself, without EsrSync — for example a native app in Swift or Kotlin, a server-side job, or a custom fetch client. The protocol package provides low-level helpers such as buildEnvEnc1Payload, sha256Hex, and schema validation; you assemble the outer envelope and send yourself. Most web and Node apps should start with the SDK only. For a full REST walkthrough, see <apiEncryptionLink>API — Envelope encryption</apiEncryptionLink>.

documents.title: EsrSync.connect options
documents.body: EsrSync.connect options Required: relayUrl, storage, onRecoveryPhrase, onConflict, and either document or documents. When apps.enabled is true, also pass appId (plus appPlatform, bundleId, and clientSecret on native when applicable). Other options have sensible defaults: Use onStatusChange for a global indicator, onDocumentStatusChange per document when using documents[], and onError for logging. See <appRegistryLink>Application registry</appRegistryLink> for registration and native fields. Full connect example (web SPA) Base URL ending in /v1, e.g. https://sync.example.com/v1 Public app id (esr_app_…) — required when relay has apps.enabled Native only: ios, android, or desktop Native only: bundle ID, package name, or desktop application ID registered for the app Native confidential clients only — when relay native.requireClientSecret is true; set via rotate-secret, never auto-assigned on app create Optional telemetry — sent as X-ESR-Client-Version Single-document shorthand — first slot is primary Multi-document: array of slots with optional documentId and adapter (first slot defaults to primary) EsrStorage implementation (createLocalStorageAdapter for web) Required — your UI. Called once with the 24-word phrase when the namespace is created. Required — your UI. Return remote, local, or cancel when versions diverge. Optional — your billing/settings UI. Called on DEVICE_LIMIT_* errors. Optional — your UI. (documentId, status) for multi-document badges. Default 2000. Delay before pushing after notifyLocalChange(). Default true. Set false for CLI tools or tests. Default true. Stores phrase in EsrStorage (consider security implications).

documents.title: Application registry (v1.3)
documents.body: Application registry (v1.3) When the relay operator enables apps.enabled, every integration must identify itself with a registered appId. Namespaces are bound to the app that created them. Full spec: <specLink>16-APP-REGISTRY.md</specLink>. REST details: <apiAppLink>API — Application registry</apiAppLink>. Two auth layers App (appId + origin or bundle) Answers: which integration may call this relay? Device token Answers: which paired device in which namespace? Unchanged from v1.2. Relay configuration apps.enabled: false (default) No app headers required — v1.2 behaviour. apps.enabled: true, operator-managed Operator registers apps via YAML seed or <operatorLink>/operator</operatorLink> portal. apps.enabled: true, self-service Developers register at <developerLink>/developer</developerLink> and verify domain or bundle ownership. Pass appId (and native fields) to EsrSync.connect(). The SDK sends X-ESR-App-Id on every relay request; browsers also send Origin automatically. Web SPA Native (iOS / Android / desktop) Registering an app App registration is separate from sync data — it does not grant access to existing namespaces. Web apps register an HTTPS origin and complete DNS TXT or well-known verification. Native apps register platform + bundle ID (iOS, Android, or desktop). Manage apps in <operatorLink>/operator</operatorLink> (operator) or <developerLink>/developer</developerLink> (self-service). Approval before API access Web: add an origin, then verify DNS TXT or HTTPS /.well-known/esr-app-verification. Status moves from pending_verification to active when verification succeeds. Native: add a bundle per platform. With native.requireManualReview: true (default), an operator must approve each bundle in <operatorLink>/operator</operatorLink> before the app becomes active. Portal labels this Pending approval — not the same as web origin verification. Native client secret Secrets are not created when you register an app. Generate one with POST .../rotate-secret or the operator/developer portal after the app is active and all bundles are approved. Required on unauthenticated routes when native.requireClientSecret: true. Pass clientSecret to EsrSync.connect() or X-ESR-Client-Secret. Check relay GET /health → apps.nativeRequireClientSecret before showing secret UI. Never embed in web builds. Pairing scope Host devices may pass allowedAppIds to startPairing to restrict guest apps (e.g. only esr_app_guest). Redeem with an unlisted appId → 403 APP_PAIRING_NOT_ALLOWED. Local development Operator sets allowLocalhostOrigins: true and registers http://localhost:'{port}' as an origin. Migrating from v1.2 Keep apps.enabled: false until all clients send app headers. Then enable the registry, register apps, and set legacyDefaultAppId for existing namespaces. See <specLink>16-APP-REGISTRY §19</specLink>.

documents.title: Multiple documents
documents.body: Multiple documents One EsrSync session can sync several independent snapshots in the same namespace. Each document has its own revision, conflict surface, and debounced push queue. Omit documentId on the first slot to use primary. Additional slots must set documentId explicitly (e.g. settings). When to use Prefer one primary document for a single app state. Split only when two JSON blobs change at different rates or need separate conflict UX.

documents.title: Document adapter
documents.body: Document adapter The adapter is the bridge between your app state and Senkronla. Use createDocumentAdapter for a quick start, or implement DocumentAdapter directly: contentType should be a vendor MIME type. See <encryptionLink>Envelope encryption</encryptionLink> for password, salt/nonce, and ENV-ENC1 details. Stable UUID v4 for this workspace — must match across devices. Human-readable name shown in device lists. Async. Returns JSON string of current app state. Async. Parses remote JSON string and applies to your store. MIME type describing your snapshot format.

documents.title: Envelope encryption (ENV-ENC1)
documents.body: Envelope encryption (ENV-ENC1) In production use createDocumentAdapter('{' encrypt: true, resolvePassword '}') or buildEnvelope('{' encrypt: true, password '}'). REST details: <apiLink>API — Envelope encryption</apiLink>. Sync password — how the SDK gets it The password belongs to your app; the SDK never generates it. Set enabled: true and resolvePassword() on DocumentAdapter.encryption(). SyncEngine calls resolvePassword() before every push/pull and passes the result to buildEnvelope / extractDocument. Typical sources: master password asked at login, OS keychain / secure enclave, workspace password chosen at setup. Paired devices must share the same password — the SDK does not sync it for you. Push / pull flow Push: buildDocument() → resolvePassword() → buildEnvelope('{' encrypt: true, password '}') → PUT .../documents/'{documentId}' Pull: GET .../head → resolvePassword() → extractDocument(envelope, password) → importDocument(json) salt and nonce are random on every push and stored inside payload — the relay does not use them; pull clients need them to decrypt Encrypted adapter example Direct buildEnvelope Recovery phrase ≠ sync password onRecoveryPhrase runs once when the namespace is created and proves relay access. Envelope encryption password is separate; if lost, encrypted remote data cannot be recovered.

documents.title: What the SDK stores locally
documents.body: What the SDK stores locally Implement EsrStorage or use createLocalStorageAdapter(prefix). Keys use '{namespaceId}:{documentId}:...' (legacy keys migrate to primary): deviceToken — shared across documents in one namespace session knownRemoteRevision — per documentId, for conflict detection recoveryPhrase — optional, if persistRecoveryPhrase is true global:clientDeviceId — generated once per app install Security Treat device tokens like session secrets. On mobile, prefer secure storage (Keychain / Keystore) by implementing EsrStorage yourself.

documents.title: EsrSync methods
documents.body: EsrSync methods Call these from your app lifecycle hooks: Examples by method Create workspace on first launch, or verify existing token. Shows recovery phrase when created=true. Full pull/push cycle. Omit documentId for all slots, or pass one id. Call on startup and reconnect; WS head_changed pulls the matching document automatically. Mark local data dirty; optional documentId scopes to one slot. Push immediately; optional documentId — use before logout. Host: returns code, qrPayload, expiresAt. Guest: redeems code, stores token, runs sync() (all documents). Recovery phrase flow. Revokes all other devices. Returns devices array and limits for settings UI. Remove another device by server deviceId (ULID). Apply operator unlock code for more device slots. Manual resolution; optional documentId when using documents[]. Current EsrSyncStatus for UI indicators. ensureNamespace() Create a workspace on first launch or verify an existing device token. sync(documentId?) Run a full pull/push cycle. Pass documentId to sync one document; omit to sync all connected documents. notifyLocalChange() Queue a debounced push after local edits. You must call this from your store subscription when data changes. flushPush() Push immediately without waiting for debounce. startPairing() Host device generates a 6-digit pairing code. You display code / QR in your UI. joinPairing(code) Guest device redeems the code you collect from the user, then syncs. recover(phrase) Restore access with the 24-word phrase from your recovery UI. listDevices() List paired devices and slot limits — render in your settings UI. revokeDevice(id) Remove another device from the workspace; refresh your device list UI. redeemUnlockCode(code) Apply an operator unlock code for extra device slots. resolveConflict(choice) Manually pick local or remote after a conflict. getStatus() Read current sync status and last error.

documents.title: Sync lifecycle
documents.body: Sync lifecycle Typical integration points in your app: App launch → ensureNamespace() then sync() (all documents) Store mutation → notifyLocalChange(documentId?) Window focus / network online → sync() or sync(documentId) for one document Logout → flushPush(documentId?) then optional disable()

documents.title: Pairing devices
documents.body: Pairing devices Both devices use the same relayUrl. The guest adapter must use the same namespaceId as the host. qrPayload follows esr://pair/v1/[namespaceId]?code=XXXXXX&exp=...&host=... for QR scanner integrations. Host device Guest device

documents.title: Handling conflicts
documents.body: Handling conflicts A conflict means the server revision advanced while you had unpushed local edits. The SDK pauses and waits for your callback. ConflictContext includes documentId plus remoteMeta for dialog copy. Implement appUi.askKeepLocalOrRemote (or equivalent) — not provided by the SDK. Manual resolution

documents.title: Live notifications
documents.body: Live notifications When enabled, the SDK opens a WebSocket to .../notifications and listens for head_changed. If WebSocket fails, it falls back to HTTP polling (ws_with_poll_fallback mode). WS only notifies — you still pull via HTTP. head_changed → automatic pull for that documentId (not a full sync()) limits_changed → slot count updated (handle in onDeviceLimit or poll limits) Optional subscribe with documentIds[] after auth_ok — filter head_changed by document

documents.title: Status values
documents.body: Status values Subscribe via onStatusChange or poll getStatus(): Polling status Ready, no operation in progress Pull or push running Local changes queued, waiting for debounce or network Waiting for onConflict user decision Network unavailable Notification WebSocket is connected

documents.title: Client error codes
documents.body: Client error codes All SDK errors are EsrError instances with a stable code string: Server-side codes (full list) are on the API page — including relay quotas (default 50 MB envelope, rate limits). Branch on error.code, not HTTP status alone. No device token yet — call ensureNamespace, joinPairing, or recover Network down — retry sync() or sync(documentId) when online Workspace already exists — use pairing or recovery instead of create User cancelled conflict dialog — local edits still pending Server revision moved — conflict flow required Workspace full — show upgrade or device management UI

documents.title: REST API reference
documents.body: JSON over HTTPS under /v1. Use this when the JavaScript SDK is not an option, or when you need server-side automation.

documents.title: Overview
documents.body: Overview All business endpoints are prefixed with /v1. Responses are JSON. Errors use a consistent shape with error.code you can switch on. Unauthenticated: POST /v1/namespaces, POST .../devices (pairing redeem), POST .../recover. Everything else needs a device token. GET /health Postman collection Import the Postman collection and environment to try every /v1 endpoint immediately. Environment variables match the HTTP examples on this page; test scripts in the Quick start folder auto-save response fields such as deviceToken, pairingCode, and notesRevision. Download collection (.json) Download local environment (localhost:8080) Download production environment template Setup Postman → Import → select both JSON files. Enable the Senkronla Relay — Local environment (top right); set relayOrigin to your relay host. Run the Quick start (run in order) folder sequentially, or send individual requests. Error response shape Errors return JSON with an error object containing code, message, and optional details (e.g. remoteMeta on REVISION_CONFLICT).

documents.title: Authentication
documents.body: Authentication After creating, pairing, or recovering a device you receive deviceToken in the response. Send it on every subsequent request: Revoked when the device is deleted or after recovery (all devices revoked). Store securely on the client. HTTP: Authorization: Bearer header WebSocket: same token in Authorization header or first auth message When apps.enabled is on, also send application headers on every /v1 route — see <apiAppLink>Application registry</apiAppLink>.

documents.title: Application registry (v1.3)
documents.body: Application registry (v1.3) Optional layer above device tokens. When enabled, each namespace belongs to exactly one registered app. App credentials answer which integration may use this relay; device tokens still gate workspace access. Full spec: <specLink>16-APP-REGISTRY.md</specLink>. Application context headers Web SPA X-ESR-App-Id plus browser Origin (must match a verified origin for that app). No client secret in browser builds. iOS / Android / desktop X-ESR-App-Id + X-ESR-Platform (ios | android | desktop) + X-ESR-Bundle-Id. Optional X-ESR-Client-Secret when native.requireClientSecret is true. Two layers — do not confuse them App context (X-ESR-App-Id + origin or native headers): which registered integration may call this relay. Device token (Authorization: Bearer dvt_…): which paired device in which namespace. Omitted on first POST /v1/namespaces; returned in the response as deviceToken. Required on all /v1 routes when enabled — including unauthenticated create, pair, and recover. Exceptions: /health, /v1/admin/*, and /v1/developer/*. WebSocket uses browser Origin at handshake time. Register the app Operator seeds YAML or uses <operatorLink>/operator</operatorLink>; in self-service mode developers use <developerLink>/developer</developerLink>. Verify origin or approve bundle Web: DNS TXT or HTTPS /.well-known/esr-app-verification. Native: register platform + bundle ID; operator approves when requireManualReview is on. App must reach active before sync calls succeed. Configure native secret (if required) When GET /health reports apps.nativeRequireClientSecret: true, generate a secret via rotate-secret after the app is active. Send as X-ESR-Client-Secret or SDK clientSecret. Send headers on every sync call Include X-ESR-App-Id (and web Origin or native platform headers) on POST /v1/namespaces, authenticated routes, and WebSocket upgrade. Add Authorization after you have a deviceToken. Namespace stays bound Create response may include appId. Later requests with a different app return 403 APP_NAMESPACE_MISMATCH. Create namespace (web client) Authenticated request (native client) Admin & developer APIs App management is out-of-band from sync routes. OpenAPI: repo root openapi.yaml (tags Applications, Developer, Admin). Operator guide: docs/OPERATOR.md. Audience Auth Web UI Operator ESR_ADMIN_TOKEN <operatorLink>/operator</operatorLink> — Apps tab Developer JWT from /developer/login <developerLink>/developer</developerLink> — when self-service enabled App-related error codes Branch on error.code. Full list in <specLink>16-APP-REGISTRY.md</specLink> and <sdkAppLink>SDK — Application registry</sdkAppLink>. Send X-ESR-App-Id — relay has app registry enabled Web client missing Origin header Origin not registered or verified for this app Namespace belongs to another app Unknown appId Operator suspended the app App not in pairing token allowedAppIds Wrong native client secret App pending verification Missing X-ESR-Platform or X-ESR-Bundle-Id Bundle ID not registered or not approved for this app Migrating from v1.2 Ship clients with app headers first, then enable apps.enabled, register apps, and set legacyDefaultAppId for existing namespaces. Details: <specLink>16-APP-REGISTRY §19</specLink>. JavaScript clients should prefer <sdkAppLink>SDK — Application registry</sdkAppLink> — pass appId to EsrSync.connect() instead of setting headers manually.

documents.title: Typical REST flow (no SDK)
documents.body: Typical REST flow (no SDK) Follow this sequence for a minimal integration: Create namespace POST /v1/namespaces with namespaceId, labels, clientDeviceId, recoveryKeyProof. Save deviceToken Persist the token from the 201 response. Check remote head GET .../documents/'{documentId}'/head/meta before every push (primary or any non-primary documentId). Push snapshot PUT .../documents/'{documentId}' with envelope. First push: no expectedRevision. Updates: must match meta revision. Poll or subscribe WebSocket head_changed or periodic GET head/meta on other devices. Pull changes GET .../head when meta revision differs from local known revision.

documents.title: Workspaces (namespaces)
documents.body: Workspaces (namespaces) One namespace per customer workspace. namespaceId must be UUID v4. Create workspace + first device Metadata, limits, head summary POST /v1/namespaces GET /v1/namespaces/[id]

documents.title: Documents
documents.body: Documents Each namespace holds one or more documents. Paths use /documents/'{documentId}'/...; primary is the default for single-document apps. Envelope schemaVersion: 2 allows any valid documentId. List all document heads in namespace Lightweight head: revision, hash, size Full envelope for import Push new snapshot (any documentId) Parametric: .../documents/'{documentId}'/... (primary alias kept). Samples below use notes as the example id; the list response also includes primary. Push examples below use encrypted Envelope encryption section envelopes (ENV-ENC1) as described there. Always compare revision before push. Mismatch → REVISION_CONFLICT with remoteMeta in details. The serialized envelope must fit within the relay's maxEnvelopeBytes limit (default 52,428,800 bytes (50 MB)). Larger payloads return 413 ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE. Unencrypted ENV-RAW1 is still supported for local development — do not use in production. GET .../documents GET .../documents/'{documentId}'/head/meta GET .../documents/'{documentId}'/head PUT .../documents/'{documentId}' (first push) PUT .../documents/'{documentId}' (update) 409 REVISION_CONFLICT

documents.title: Envelope encryption (ENV-ENC1)
documents.body: Envelope encryption (ENV-ENC1) In production, application data must travel inside an encrypted ESR-DOC1 envelope (ENV-ENC1 inner payload). The relay stores an opaque string only. If you use the JavaScript SDK, see also <sdkLink>SDK — Envelope encryption</sdkLink>. What is the sync password? The encryption password is an application secret that locks the envelope. Senkronla does not generate it and never sends it to the relay. You provide it — master password, workspace sync password, vault PIN derivative, etc. The client uses it on every push and pull (via resolvePassword() in the SDK). All paired devices must know the same password; pairing and recovery do not transfer it automatically. Do not mix these secrets Sync password — ENV-ENC1 encryption; app-provided; never sent to server 24-word recovery phrase — namespace access proof; does not decrypt envelopes by itself deviceToken — relay API session; unrelated to envelope encryption demo-sync-passphrase — documentation HTTP/Postman samples only What is inside payload? The outer envelope sets contentMagic: ENV-ENC1. The payload string is JSON the relay does not parse: salt + nonce — random per push; not secret; carried with ciphertext so pull clients can decrypt ciphertext — AES-256-GCM encrypted application JSON kdf / iterations — PBKDF2-SHA256, default 600000 Building envelopes over REST (no SDK) Use buildEnvEnc1Payload from @senkronla/protocol, then set contentSha256 = sha256Hex(payload) on the outer envelope. Never put the password in HTTP requests. Example: inner payload + PUT body Recovery ≠ sync password POST .../recover only issues a new deviceToken. Envelopes encrypted with a lost sync password cannot be opened — plan separate password backup UX.

documents.title: Devices & recovery
documents.body: Devices & recovery Pairing and recovery endpoints do not require an existing token (recovery uses phrase proof instead). Host generates 6-digit code Guest redeems code → new token List devices + limits Remove a device (cannot remove last device) Phrase proof → new token, all other devices revoked POST .../pairing-tokens POST .../devices (pairing redeem) GET .../devices DELETE .../devices/[deviceId] POST .../recover Recovery revokes all devices POST .../recover invalidates every existing device token in the workspace. Plan your UX accordingly.

documents.title: Limits & unlock
documents.body: Limits & unlock Operators set freeDeviceLimit per deployment. purchasedSlots increase maxDevices. Current limits and canAddDevice flag Redeem unlock code for more slots GET .../limits POST .../unlock

documents.title: WebSocket notifications
documents.body: WebSocket notifications Connect to the notifications URL with the device token. Subprotocol: esr-notifications-v1. Messages are notifications only — always fetch document data via HTTP GET. After auth_ok, send '{"type":"subscribe","documentIds":["primary","settings"]}' to filter events (optional). head_changed — includes documentId; pull that document when convenient limits_changed — device slot count changed WebSocket messages

documents.title: Relay quotas & size limits
documents.body: Relay quotas & size limits The relay operator configures these in config.yaml or ESR_* environment variables. If nothing is set, the defaults below apply automatically — limits are on by default. Maximum envelope size Measured on the full serialized ESR-DOC1 JSON at push time. Default: 52,428,800 bytes (50 MB). Configure with sync.maxEnvelopeBytes or ESR_MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES. Rate limits (defaults) Sliding-window counters in PostgreSQL. Exempt from the general IP quota: /health, /metrics, and WebSocket .../notifications. All API requests Document push (PUT .../documents/'{documentId}') Guest pairing redeem Pairing code generation Recovery 300 / minute 120 / hour 20 / hour 30 / hour 5 / hour Client IP Device Namespace Namespace Namespace 1 minute 1 hour 1 hour 1 hour 1 hour Quota in responses When limits.rateLimit.enabled is true, most /v1 responses return quota info via HTTP headers and, on some routes, a JSON rateLimits object. HTTP headers General IP — RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset Document PUT — RateLimit-PutDocument-* Recovery and pairing — RateLimit-Recover-*, RateLimit-Pair-*, RateLimit-PairingToken-* JSON body (rateLimits) Some success responses also include a top-level rateLimits object. Keys (internal action ids): global_ip, put_document, recover, pair_device, pairing_token Each value includes: action, limit, remaining, resetAfterSeconds, windowSeconds Every successful PUT .../documents/'{documentId}' decrements put_document (not only the first push). Routes with rateLimits in the body Document PUT GET .../head/meta and GET .../head GET .../documents POST .../recover POST .../pairing-tokens POST .../devices (pair redeem) No body object (headers may still apply) POST /namespaces, GET .../devices, limits/unlock, DELETE 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED Retry-After header and error.details.rateLimit (single quota object, same fields as above) No top-level rateLimits on errors Example shapes

documents.title: Error codes
documents.body: Error codes Always branch on error.code. Common codes: Fix request body fields Re-pair or recover — token invalid or revoked Wrong recovery phrase proof Show upgrade / unlock UI User must remove a device Check namespaceId No push yet — expected on first pull Namespace taken — pair or recover instead Re-read head/meta, run conflict UX Envelope exceeds maxEnvelopeBytes (default 50 MB) — shrink snapshot or ask operator to raise limit Fix envelope schema or hash Quota exceeded — Retry-After, RateLimit-* headers, and error.details.rateLimit (remaining is 0) Code expired or wrong — generate a new one Invalid or expired unlock code Path documentId format invalid Too many documents in namespace — raise maxDocumentsPerNamespace or delete unused ids documentId not in server allowlist Envelope documentId must match URL path
